# The build directive belongs to the package, not to a file: any file may carry
# it, and a second one anywhere in the package names the first.
#
# The rule it replaces asked a question about a file -- "output declarations
# only permitted in main file" -- and counted nothing, so a package could hold
# as many directives as it had files: each was built, and a target named twice
# with different options was whichever came out of the merge last.

sngl check pkg
stdout 'ok'

! sngl check twice
stderr 'twice[/\\]b.sngl:1:1: output is already declared for this package at .*twice[/\\]a.sngl:4:1'

-- pkg/app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import app "sngl:app"

component main ui {
    text(value="hi")
}

app.window {
    main
}
-- pkg/targets.sngl --
output {
    go {
        bubbletea()
    }
}
-- twice/a.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import app "sngl:app"

output {
    go {
        bubbletea()
    }
}

component main ui {
    text(value="hi")
}

app.window {
    main
}
-- twice/b.sngl --
output {
    go {
        bubbletea()
    }
}
